fields.summary: Forgot password tokens should be invalidated when account email address changes or a new token is requested

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
We should only be accepting tokens sent to an account's current email address, so when a user's email account is updated, we should invalidate tokens used in password reset (forgotten password) links sent to the old address. (It would be worth also having a look for  any other similar tokens that may need similar treatment.)

We should also be removing existing tokens if a new one is generated (ie another forgot password request for the account is received).

Given the (default) short life of such tokens and the fact that they are single use, these are fairly edge case, but is a valid fix to comply with security best practice. Taking that into account along with the low risk of being an exploitable issue, I've marked this as a security benefit, and not assigned a security level.

For consistency, we should also invalidate forgot password tokens if the password is changed, regardless of method..

fields.summary: Define a password length upper limit to future-proof from hashing denial of service risks

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
We should mitigate any future risks of [long password denial of service.|https://www.acunetix.com/vulnerabilities/web/long-password-denial-of-service/]

After doing a deep dive into how password resets work in our various authentication plugins, +*this does not appear to be a current security risk*+ {*}while bcrypt is used as the hashing algorithm{*}.

All authentication plugins except for OAuth use moodlelib's [hash_internal_user_password|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/lib/moodlelib.php#L4797] method, which utilises PHP's [password_hash|https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.password-hash.php] function using the default hashing algorithm. Currently, that is bcrypt, which (as mentioned in the docs) truncates passwords after 72 characters automatically and therefore effectively mitigates this risk. I confirmed this was the case in practice (both via forgot password and preferences).

I would suggest that we create a constant containing a reasonable upper limit (as is [recommened by OWASP|https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/blob/master/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.md#maximum-password-lengths]), which is applied as part of {_}hash_internal_user_password(){_}, so that when we change our hashing algorithm, it does not inadvertently introduce a login DoS vulnerability into Moodle. *This will become critical once MDL-67390 lands, as SHA-512 does not perform the same truncating as bcrypt.* We should also ensure that password peppers are factored in (introduced in MDL-67774), to ensure that peppers are not counted when validating the length of the password.

Regarding OAuth authentication plugin password resets, the hashing algorithms used are currently either MD5, SHA1 or none, and according to the same OWASP docs, using "faster" hashing algorithms to mitigate length concerns is a valid use case, therefore this does not appear to pose a denial of service vulnerability. I would suggest we also look into whether it would be suitable to update that with a limit while we are making these changes.

In addition to updating the limit in the backend, we also need to consider the following for any cases where the user can input, set or change their password:
 * Updating the length limit on any password input fields.
 * Applying frontend validation on length.
 * Applying backend validation on length.

Currently the bcrypt truncation occurs silently, so none of the above have been implemented in the existing functionality.

I have marked this as an improvement, but think we should consider backporting some or all of this to any relevant security branches, if it does not raise any breaking changes/blockers that would prevent it.

_Writeup/testing/investigation by_ [~accountid:5ccb99144253ab0e29348c22]{_}, after receiving an initial report re potential login DoS on forgot password reset by [~accountid:5e85789f9126d30c240014c9]  (SF case 00091645).{_}

*Initial test results:*

Some quick test results for various hashing methods. The first set of methods use SHA512 with 10,000 rounds to generate a single password of varying lengths:
{code:java}Length: 8, Time: 0.005295991897583 seconds
Length: 16, Time: 0.0082888603210449 seconds
Length: 25, Time: 0.0095119476318359 seconds
Length: 50, Time: 0.0093979835510254 seconds
Length: 100, Time: 0.016441106796265 seconds
Length: 200, Time: 0.017743825912476 seconds
Length: 300, Time: 0.033573865890503 seconds
Length: 400, Time: 0.037233114242554 seconds
Length: 500, Time: 0.043007135391235 seconds
Length: 600, Time: 0.049973011016846 seconds
Length: 700, Time: 0.081401109695435 seconds
Length: 800, Time: 0.066431999206543 seconds
Length: 900, Time: 0.10497498512268 seconds
Length: 1000, Time: 0.099220991134644 seconds{code}
The second tests compare the time to generate 1,000 hashes for randomly generated 1,000 digit passwords
{code:java}Generating 1000 hashes using bcrypt...
Cost: 4, Time: 1.110445022583 seconds
Cost: 10, Time: 68.429219961166 seconds{code}
As expected Bcrypt hashing times for passwords of length 1000 are more or less the same for smaller lengths (because of the 72 digit cut off).

However, the SHA2 class of hashes do take an extended period of time with long passwords.

 
{code:java}Generating 1000 hashes using SHA256...
Rounds: 5000, Time: 138.83062696457 seconds
Rounds: 10000, Time: 256.1211771965 seconds
Generating 1000 hashes using SHA512...
Rounds: 5000, Time: 92.857749223709 seconds
Rounds: 10000, Time: 164.08723402023 seconds
{code}
 

Therefore when when we change to SHA512 for password hashes, we should limit the maximum password length. A max length of *128 characters* seems a good compromise. It exceeds NIST (as per NIST Special Publication 800-63B) recommendation, and allows for multi word passphrases.

Rerunning the test to generate 1000 passwords hashes using 128 character random passwords using SHA512 achieves acceptable results.
{code:java}Generating 1000 hashes using SHA512...
Rounds: 5000, Time: 12.569887876511 seconds
Rounds: 10000, Time: 25.713526010513 seconds{code}

fields.summary: File upload should have a progress bar in the file manager

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

components.name: Filepicker
components.description: The GUI for picking files

fields.description:
Summary:
Add an upload progress bar to filemanager-triggered file uploads in the file picker.

Problem:
When a user browses and selects a file to upload through the file picker into a filemanager field, the only feedback shown is a spinning wheel with no indication of progress. For large files this leaves the user unsure whether the upload is proceeding or has stalled.

Current behaviour:
The filemanager shows a generic loading spinner for the whole upload, with no percentage or progress indication, unlike drag-and-drop uploads into the same filemanager, which already show a progress bar.

Expected behaviour:
When uploading a file via "Add..." > "Upload a file" into a filemanager field, a progress bar is shown and updated as the upload proceeds, consistent with the existing drag-and-drop upload progress bar.

Value:
Gives users confidence that a large upload is progressing, reduces support/confusion around "stuck" uploads, and brings the filepicker upload flow to parity with the existing drag-and-drop upload experience.

Scope:
In scope: uploads triggered via the file picker's "Upload a file" tab into a filemanager field (for example the "New picture" field on Edit profile, or any filemanager form element).
Out of scope: uploads triggered via the file picker in other contexts that have no filemanager to render a progress bar into, for example inserting an image via the Atto editor's "Insert image" > "Browse repositories" flow. Those continue to use the existing upload flow with no progress bar, and must continue to work without errors.

Acceptance criteria:
- Uploading a file into a filemanager field via the file picker shows a progress bar with a percentage while the upload is in progress.
- The progress bar clears once the upload finishes (success or failure) and the filemanager returns to its normal state.
- Uploading an unsupported file type still shows the "File type not accepted" dialogue, and after dismissing it the file picker is shown again with the Attachment field so the user can pick another file, without needing to reopen "Add...".
- Uploading via the Atto editor's "Insert image" > "Browse repositories" flow continues to work with no JavaScript errors (no progress bar is expected there, since there is no filemanager in that context).
- Existing filemanager behaviours (overwrite, create shortcut, cancel, select existing file, edit file) are unaffected.

Notes:
Implementation rewrites the upload transport in public/repository/filepicker.js from the legacy YUI Y.io transport to native XMLHttpRequest + FormData, since XHR upload progress events are needed to drive the progress bar. Progress bar rendering/state lives in public/lib/form/filemanager.js. Both files are legacy YUI JavaScript modules, not AMD.

Tested on Moodle main (5.3dev, build 20260708). Behat coverage exercised: upload_file_type.feature, overwrite_file.feature, create_shortcut.feature, cancel_add_file.feature, cancel_close_filepicker.feature, upload/tests/behat/upload_file.feature, select_file.feature, edit_file.feature — all pass.

Peer review during this pass found and fixed two issues in the submitted patch:
- The file picker dialogue was being hidden before the upload result was known, with nothing to re-show it if the upload failed (for example a rejected file type), forcing users to reopen "Add..." to retry. Fixed by re-showing the dialogue on upload error.
- The AJAX response handler parsed the server response with JSON.parse and no error handling, unlike the original code. A non-JSON HTTP 200 response (for example debug output preceding the JSON on a site with developer debugging enabled) would throw an uncaught exception and leave the progress bar stuck. Fixed by wrapping the parse in a try/catch with the same friendly exception dialogue the rest of the file uses elsewhere.

This caused problems for one of our staff members when we used this config setting on a local plugin. They made multiple config changes including to a limited-length field. One way to avoid this problem and simultaneously make the UI nicer would be to apply the length limit client-side, i.e. use JavaScript to:

fields.summary: Disconnect from database while waiting for session lock

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

components.name: Database SQL/XMLDB
components.description: This component type is for all database issues involving specific DBMSs, SQL and XMLDB. (It is not the Moodle Database activity).

components.name: Performance
components.description: All bugs to do with performance bugs and improvements

fields.description:
On installations with a large number of concurrent users a common problem is lock contention for the session write lock. As a consequence a lot of requests may end up waiting on a session write lock. While doing so they keep the database connection open which is opened at the beginning of handling a request. As waiting for a session lock can take several seconds or depending on config even minutes (think that's the default), this can lead to database problems due to the large number of open connections.

Installing tools like ProxySQL or PgBouncer on the webservers can help alleviate some of this problem, but to avoid a tipping point this patch proposes to disconnect from the database entirely if the wait for the session lock has gone on for 2 seconds, and reconnects to the database once the session lock has been acquired.

The current patch only implements this behavior for the redis session handler and mysqli_native. So if there is interest one could add support for the same behavior to other session handlers and database systems, although the code works as-is on all systems and simply does not do the reconnect if it is not supported by the underlying database system.

fields.summary: When replying to a forum post, the "Advanced" button should not pass the data in the URL as query parameters

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Currently, when replying to a forum post, the user is presented with a simple textarea for the message body. The user can, however, click the "Advanced" button, which will load a new page with more detailed options. The existing post data – what the user has already entered in the reply box – is passed to this page through query parameters in the URL in order to auto-fill the response box. However, this can cause issues in some setups.

A very similar functionality exists when creating a new forum topic (rather than replying to an existing one). In this case, clicking "Advanced" handles the page transition appropriately, passing the data as form data in the request body. The way this works should be duplicated for forum responses.

To duplicate:
 * Create a forum activity
 * Add a new topic
 * Add a subject and some text to the message box
 * Clicked "Advanced"
 * Note that the data is passed through the request body in order to autofill the box on the next page
 * Submit the forum topic
 * Click on the posted topic to view the thread
 * Click "Reply" and add a few lines of text
 * Click "Advanced"
 * Note how the data is passed through the URL as query parameters in order to autofill the box on the next page

The issue with using query parameters here is that control characters in URLs can cause problems with some setups. Lighttp, for example, will return a 400 error by default for any URL containing a control character, such as a linefeed + carriage return (%0D%0A). In this case, users can not reply to a forum post with text containing multiple lines unless they first click the "Advanced" button.
